clue.text: One of life's tenser moments concealing some Shakespearean light relief

indicators.note: the phrase about life's tense moments holds a short run of letters within its words, straddling the apostrophe-s

explanation.surface: A tense moment in life is eased by a touch of comedy from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing some' tells you the answer sits inside 'life's tenser'. Feste is the clown in Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The singing clown of Twelfth Night supplies the play's comic interludes.

clue.text: First fairly apt current figure of speech in transmitted copy

indicators.note: the first letter of the word fairly is taken

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a simile is a figure of speech comparing one thing to another

explanation.surface: A fitting comparison appears early in a document sent by wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apt' only colours the surface, describing the simile. A facsimile is a fax, a copy sent down the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A fax is an exact reproduction sent electronically over a telephone line.

clue.text: Some serpentine verse of Lawrence

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence wrote a well-known poem about a creature at his water-trough in Sicily, titled after the animal

explanation.surface: A remark about winding lines in a poem by Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence's poem about a reptile drinking at his trough is named for that legless creature.

clue.text: A man of letters '

parts.note: usually a learned writer, here read literally as someone who writes correspondence

explanation.surface: A description of a literary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe is an artefact of the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistoler is a writer of epistles, that is, correspondence, so literally a man of letters.

clue.text: Get newssheet returning to provide pocket-size reading

parts.note: a newssheet is a newspaper, or paper
returning means coming back

explanation.surface: Fetch a newspaper on the way home for something small to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-covered books are small enough to slip into a pocket.

clue.text: Sign for printer to turn up lip and brag

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word lip is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to crow is to boast or brag

explanation.surface: An instruction to curl one's lip and boast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' turns LIP into PIL. The pilcrow is the paragraph mark ¶.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilcrow is the paragraph mark used in typesetting and proofreading.

clue.text: Larcenous as Goldings bird

parts.note: William Golding's novel names its hero after a bird, the martin, with a nickname meaning thief before it

explanation.surface: A thieving bird from a Golding novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Golding's novel is Pincher Martin; a martin is a bird, and a pincher is one who pinches, or steals.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for to steal, so one who pinches is a thief, as the novel's hero is.

clue.text: "Englishwoman should never, he told her" (Elizabeth Taylor, A Game of Hide-and-Seek)

definitions.text: "Englishwoman should never, he told her" (Elizabeth Taylor, A Game of Hide-and-Seek)

parts.words: "Englishwoman should never, he told her" (Elizabeth Taylor, A Game of Hide-and-Seek)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing after never: the solver supplies the Latin dance it names from the novel

explanation.surface: A quotation from Elizabeth Taylor's novel with its verb left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a fill-in-the-gap quotation: the missing word is a Cuban ballroom dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap in the quotation is filled by a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: First-class backing for depth in Scoop setting

parts.note: an abyss is a great depth
taken as written

indicators.note: backing means the letters for first-class are written in reverse

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-class

explanation.surface: A top-class depth gauge for the setting of a news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the A1-style letters for first-class. Evelyn Waugh's novel Scoop is set in Ishmaelia, modelled on the African country where Waugh worked as a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's fictional Ishmaelia in Scoop was based on the African country he had covered, now Ethiopia.

clue.text: Elegiac sound from distinguished portraitist?

indicators.note: the sound is taken from the start of the painter's name, leaving its ending behind

parts.note: Sir Godfrey Kneller was the leading portrait painter in late Stuart England

explanation.surface: A mournful note from an eminent painter of portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the start of KNELLER, dropping ER. A knell is the bell tolled at a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolling bell for a death or funeral is a mournful, lamenting sound.

clue.text: Walter the poet's Paris porte

definitions.meaning: Walter of ... was a twelfth-century French poet who wrote the Latin epic Alexandreis
one of the gates in the old ring of Paris, now a métro station, bears this name

explanation.surface: A Parisian gateway linked to a poet called Walter.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Latin poet is known by his French home town, which also names a gate on the Paris ring road.

clue.text: Said to be principal children's writer

indicators.note: said to be means the word for principal is spoken, giving a name that sounds like it

parts.note: principal means main

explanation.surface: A claim that someone is the leading author for young readers.
explanation.walkthrough: William Mayne wrote many novels for children.
explanation.definitionFit: William Mayne was a prolific British author of books for young readers.

clue.text: Plainer Tale from (Kipling's) Hills has sluggish content

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words Plainer Tale

explanation.surface: A Kipling-style story from the hills with a slow-moving plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Kipling's Plain Tales from the Hills; the answer runs across 'plaINER Tale'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inactive or slow to move is lethargic and torpid.

clue.text: Dry run satirizing Dryden

definitions.meaning: a practice performance before the real thing
the Duke of Buckingham's 1671 comedy mocked Dryden's heroic plays

explanation.surface: A trial attempt at mocking the poet Dryden.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice run is a trial, and Buckingham's burlesque play of that title parodied Dryden as Bayes.

clue.text: New lingo we expect from poet and novelist

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of lingo and we are made into something fresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh language is what we look for from a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LINGO WE. Jean Ingelow was a Victorian poet and novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Ingelow was a Victorian writer of verse and fiction.

clue.text: Foreseeable career path for little women

definitions.text: Foreseeable career path for little women

parts.words: Foreseeable career path for little women
parts.note: Louisa May Alcott's Little Women was followed by a sequel whose title describes the girls grown up and married

explanation.surface: Young girls' likely future, in the conventional view.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the second part of Alcott's Little Women was published separately under this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcott's sequel to Little Women shows the March sisters as married wives.

clue.text: Layback time for Chatterton

definitions.meaning: the moment of getting even with someone
Thomas Chatterton wrote a burletta with this title in 1770

explanation.surface: The moment to settle scores with the poet Chatterton.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting even is retaliation, and Chatterton's comic opera bore that title.

clue.text: Havana visa badly needed for Hindu sectarian

indicators.note: badly means the letters of Havana and visa are put together wrongly, rearranged

parts.note: the city name as the setter needed it, one A short of its printed form

explanation.surface: A Hindu devotee needs a travel permit for Cuba's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges HAVANA VISA, but that has one A more than the answer: the setter's slip. A Vaishnava is a worshipper of Vishnu.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vaishnava belongs to the branch of Hinduism devoted to Vishnu.

clue.text: Stargazer may come to doting end

indicators.note: may come to suggests the letters of doting end can turn into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomer might end up besotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may come to' rearranges DOTING END. Sir Arthur Eddington was a leading astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Eddington was an astronomer and astrophysicist.

clue.text: A journey for Agate?

parts.note: the critic James Agate published his diaries in volumes titled Ego, so a trip in his company is a trip through his self

explanation.surface: Travel plans for a gemstone, or for the critic James Agate.
explanation.walkthrough: James Agate's nine volumes of diaries are called Ego; the answer means self-indulgent behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-indulgent exercise is a vanity trip, and Agate's diaries were titled Ego.

clue.text: Winged creature from Lewis

definitions.meaning: the flying horse of Greek myth
C. Day Lewis published ... and Other Poems in 1957, its title poem named for the mythical horse

explanation.surface: A creature with wings from the work of Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: The flying horse of Greek legend gives its name to C. Day Lewis's 1957 collection.

clue.text: Bandit badly barding

indicators.note: badly means the letters of barding are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An outlaw who writes poetry poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges BARDING.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw who robs travellers is a highwayman or bandit.

clue.text: Novelist graduate manages to contain impulses

indicators.note: manages to contain means the graduate letters hold the next word inside them

parts.note: BS is Bachelor of Science, a graduate
urges are impulses

explanation.surface: A writer with a degree keeps desires in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Burgess wrote A Clockwork Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Burgess was the author of A Clockwork Orange and many other novels.

clue.text: "Though this catering — be bold to call it wicked" (Milton, Colasterion)

definitions.text: "Though this catering — be bold to call it wicked" (Milton, Colasterion)

parts.words: "Though this catering — be bold to call it wicked" (Milton, Colasterion)
parts.note: a quotation from Milton's pamphlet with a word missing at the dash: a contemptuous term for a pettifogging lawyer

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton's Colasterion with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Milton's sentence with his scornful word for a trader in legal quibbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's sneering term means a petty, venal lawyer who deals in legal quibbles.

clue.text: Writer to stay temporarily in box

definitions.meaning: to stay as a ... in someone's house
a shooting box is a small country house for sportsmen

explanation.surface: An author spending a short time in a theatre box.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'box' here is a shooting box, a small house used during the shooting season.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lodge is a novelist; one may lodge as a paying guest; and a small hunting house is a box.

clue.text: Trollope's country seat

parts.note: Anthony Trollope's novel takes its title from a farm estate at the centre of a disputed will

explanation.surface: A rural estate belonging to Trollope.
explanation.walkthrough: Trollope's novel Orley Farm turns on the inheritance of this property.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's Orley Farm centres on the forged codicil that secures the estate.

clue.text: Beauty found in the length and breadth of Greece

indicators.note: found in means the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.words: the length and breadth of Greece

explanation.surface: Loveliness discovered all across Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'tHE LENgth'. Helen of Troy was the great beauty of Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy is the archetypal beautiful woman of Greek myth.

clue.text: Funnily enough there's some Irish in the boy at Cockpen

definitions.text: Funnily enough there's some Irish in the boy at Cockpen

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for Irish goes inside the word for boy

parts.note: a boy is a lad
IR is an abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: It is odd to find something Irish in a Scottish lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Laird o' Cockpen is a Scottish song by Lady Nairne; a laird is a Scottish landowner, so Irish letters inside him are 'funnily enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish landed proprietor is the title figure of the song about Cockpen.

clue.text: Nina Bawden's lived back at the seaside

indicators.note: back means the word lived is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Where Nina Bawden once lived, by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LIVED round. Nina Bawden's first novel was Devil by the Sea, hence 'at the seaside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina Bawden's 1957 novel Devil by the Sea names this evil spirit in its title.

clue.text: Actress in process of describing screenwriter

indicators.note: process means the letters of actress in are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer in the middle of describing a film writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' rearranges ACTRESS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenarist writes scenarios, the scripts for films.

clue.text: Writers offering attempts first hidden

indicators.note: hidden means the letters for first are tucked inside the word for attempts

parts.note: essays are attempts
first is abbreviated 1st, here read as IST

explanation.surface: Authors offering their early tries kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is printed in short as 1st, the digit read as a letter I; 'hidden' tucks it inside the word for attempts, before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors of short prose pieces on a subject are writers.

clue.text: Tennyson's rough sailor's lad in the forest

definitions.meaning: Tennyson's poem opens on Enoch, an orphaned rough sailor's lad
the woodland setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: Tennyson's tough seaman's boy among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch Arden is Tennyson's sailor hero, and Arden is the Warwickshire woodland of As You Like It.
